The **2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election** was a local government election held on **3 May 2012** to elect councillors to **Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council** in Greater Manchester, England. The election was part of the wider **2012 UK local elections**, which saw contests across many parts of England, Scotland, and Wales.

### **Key Details:**
- **Council Type:** Metropolitan Borough Council (part of Greater Manchester)
- **Total Seats on Council:** 63 (all seats up for election in 2012, as it was a full reorganisation)
- **Election System:** First-past-the-post (FPTP) in single-member wards
- **Turnout:** Around **32.3%** (slightly lower than the national average for local elections that year)

### **Political Context:**
- The election took place under the **Coalition Government** (Conservative-Liberal Democrat) led by **David Cameron**.
- **Stockport had been under no overall control (NOC)** since 2011, with the **Liberal Democrats** as the largest party but losing their majority.
- The **Labour Party** was performing strongly in local elections nationwide in 2012, capitalising on dissatisfaction with austerity measures.

### **Results Summary:**
| **Party**            | **Seats Before** | **Seats After** | **Change** | **Vote Share** |
|----------------------|------------------|-----------------|------------|----------------|
| **Liberal Democrats** | 28               | 21              | **-7**     | 28.5%          |
| **Labour**           | 21               | 26              | **+5**     | 33.8%          |
| **Conservative**     | 14               | 16              | **+2**     | 31.2%          |
| **Green Party**      | 0                | 0               | **±0**     | 4.2%           |
| **UKIP**             | 0                | 0               | **±0**     | 1.3%           |
| **Others/Indep.**    | 0                | 0               | **±0**     | 1.0%           |

- **Labour became the largest party**, gaining 5 seats, but **no party won a majority** (32 seats needed for control).
- The **Liberal Democrats remained the second-largest party** despite losing 7 seats.
- The **Conservatives made minor gains**, increasing by 2 seats.
- The **Green Party** and **UKIP** contested seats but won none.

### **Aftermath & Control of the Council:**
- **No Overall Control (NOC) continued**, meaning the council operated under a **minority administration**.
- **Labour formed a minority administration**, relying on support from other parties (likely the Lib Dems or independents) to pass budgets and policies.
- The political landscape remained **highly competitive**, with Stockport often switching between Labour and Liberal Democrat control in subsequent years.

### **Notable Ward Results:**
- **Labour gains were concentrated in traditionally working-class areas** like **Brinnington & Central, Reddish North, and Edgeley & Cheadle Heath**.
- The **Lib Dems held on in strongholds like Cheadle & Gatley, Marple North, and Heald Green**.
- The **Conservatives made gains in more affluent suburban wards** such as **Hazel Grove and Stepping Hill**.

### **Significance:**
- The election reflected **national trends**, with Labour benefiting from mid-term anti-government sentiment.
- It marked a **decline for the Liberal Democrats**, who were suffering from their role in the Coalition Government.
- Stockport remained a **key battleground** in Greater Manchester, often seen as a **bellwether** for national political shifts.

### **Subsequent Elections:**
- In **2014**, Labour **gained control** of Stockport Council for the first time since 2004.
- The **Liberal Democrats regained control in 2019**, only to lose it again to Labour in **2022**.
